topic: Never answer an offer with いいです
style: Calm and direct, like a friend correcting you kindly. Slow on the Japanese.

script.hook: Someone offers you tea, and you say, いいです. They may hear, no thank you.
points: Here is the slip. A host holds out a cup, and you say, いいです, thinking, that sounds good. You meant yes.
But after an offer, いいです can also read as, I am fine, no need. The host smiles and puts the cup down.
The fix is simple. Say, はい、おねがいします, which is, yes please. Or say, いただきます, I will gladly have it. One exception. If someone asks, いいですか, is this okay, then いいです really is yes.
script.takeaway: So when it is an offer, say yes with real words, not with いいです.
script.cta: Save this, you will want it later.

blocks.jp:
お茶、どうですか。
いいです。

items.text: いいですか → いいです = yes

cover.sub: いいです after an offer

social.caption:
Someone offers you something, you say いいです, and they may hear no thank you.

いいです (ii desu) after an offer can read as good, or as I am fine without it.

Say yes clearly:
はい、お願いします (hai, onegai shimasu) = yes, please.
いただきます (itadakimasu) = I will gladly have it.

One exception: if someone asks いいですか (is this okay?), いいです really is yes.

Save this, you will want it later.
